parsed.wine_summary:
Within the Penfolds Bin hierarchy, Bin 2 occupies an unusual niche: it's Mataro-led in a portfolio dominated by Shiraz and Cabernet. The wine was revived in 2003 after a long hiatus, drawing on McLaren Vale's deep reservoir of old-vine Mataro — plantings that survived the vine-pull schemes of the 1970s and 80s because the vines were too gnarled and unproductive to bother removing. Those surviving vines now produce tiny yields of intensely concentrated fruit.

The Shiraz component (the secondary grape here despite sometimes appearing first on labels) provides the structural backbone — dark fruit, tannin grip, and aromatic lift — while Mataro brings the wine's defining character: earthy, meaty, with dried herb and a dusty tannin texture that reads more Mediterranean than Australian. Penfolds treats this as a mid-tier Bin wine, meaning it gets serious oak treatment and blending attention from the winemaking team, but it doesn't carry the price premium of Bin 28 or Bin 128.

Some sites sit over terra rossa on limestone, which adds a mineral, almost chalky quality to the tannin structure. The warm days and cool maritime evenings preserve acidity in what would otherwise be a very ripe, high-alcohol wine, and that diurnal range is what allows the Mataro to develop its characteristic savory, dried-herb complexity rather than tipping into pure jammy fruit.
